answer: A decentralized network resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to accumulate witnessed work before its voice carries weight. A new account starts at zero, with no influence granted on arrival. The protocol treats this unproven state as a distant nebula: visible from afar, but no single particle moves consensus. Standing grows through a long voyage across epochs. Established identities rise like a mesa, solid from years of checked labor. Because voting weight follows witnessed tenure rather than key count, synthetic accounts stay in the nebula while genuine contributors stand firm.
